comparator.name: South and Southeast Asian Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The nine retained first-year components total 60 EC. Faculty Article 3.2 and the current programme confirm 30 EC of open study, now listed once: 90 supported listed EC. The other 90 EC is described in the annual catalogue but is not certified as a complete revised-cohort route. Reading South and Southeast Asia, 5 EC, still explicitly requires Area Studies; the revised first-year groups omit it. Modern Histories includes academic skills, but neither its description nor the regulations establish an accepted replacement. English Philosophy of Science is confirmed. Language study continues in the same sequence; Seminar II requires at least 45 first-year EC including Seminar I; Seminar III, study abroad and the thesis have further progression rules. The actual linked public graphic has revised first-year content and places Reading in year three, with Economies, Literatures, Philosophy of Science and Humanities in a Digital World in year two; the annual catalogue instead places Reading in year two and uses different core/choice groups. The graphic has no EC labels and a current-year/next-year caveat. Its 2526 URL path alone does not establish its cohort. Neither source resolves the absent Area Studies prerequisite. No exemption is inferred from a missing entry or generic permission process.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s degree studies South and Southeast Asia, with particular attention to India, Tibet and Indonesia. Students study regional history, religion, culture and politics alongside Hindi, Indonesian, Sanskrit or Tibetan.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The revised first year and 30 EC of elective study are confirmed, giving 90 EC listed here. The published later-year schedules differ, and a prerequisite for the required Reading course remains unclear. These requirements need reconciliation before a complete pathway and a full UCR comparison can be assessed.

curriculum.limitation: This partial record lists the first-year 60 EC, illustrated with Hindi and eligible choices, plus 30 EC of open study. The public graphic and catalogue differ on later-year requirements, including when Reading is taken. Its entry requirement and the complete route to the thesis are not certified for this intake.

componentNotes.sseas-y1-modern-history: Studies colonial states, economies and knowledge, nationalism and decolonisation in South and Southeast Asia, with compulsory academic-skills tutorials for students in this degree.
componentNotes.sseas-y1-premodern-history: Studies regional histories from about 3500 BCE to 1850, connecting settlement, states and cultures through migration, trade and conquest, including Indianisation, Islamisation and colonisation.
componentNotes.sseas-y1-culture: Studies nations, communities and identities through heritage, memory, religion, gender, caste, migration, diaspora and globalisation, using cases across the region.
componentNotes.sseas-y1-politics-economy: Studies political and economic development since about 1950, including democracy and authoritarianism, minorities, growth, religion and politics, and civil society.
componentNotes.sseas-y1-classical-seminar: Studies manuscripts, monuments, religious objects, kingship and epics as shared cultural heritage, alongside library, presentation and writing skills. Positive first-year study advice requires at least 45 EC including a pass in this seminar.
componentNotes.sseas-y1-religion: This example chooses Islam from the three options: Islam, Buddhism or Hindu religions. It studies historical and modern Islam through texts, ritual, law, arts, Sufism and political movements; it is not confined to Southeast Asia.
componentNotes.sseas-y1-hindi-one: Introduces Hindi through listening, speaking, reading and writing, including Devanagari script, authentic materials and communicative practice. Hindi illustrates one of four language sequences; students keep the same language across the first two years.
componentNotes.sseas-y1-hindi-two: Continues the four language skills and practical communication. Entry requires successful completion of Hindi 1; exceptional entry requires individual advice and is not assumed here.
componentNotes.sseas-y1-elective: Classics of Asia is the illustrated 5 EC regional choice. The other listed options are Asian Societies in Motion and Power, Development and Conflict in Asia. Classics studies the transmission, interpretation and afterlives of influential Asian texts, including South Asian works.
componentNotes.sseas-open-study: The degree reserves 30 EC for a minor or other permitted elective study. Individual packages need approval, sufficient level and no overlap with compulsory study; normally no more than 10 EC is introductory and at least 10 EC is advanced. Recognised full 30 EC minors at Leiden, Delft or Erasmus have an approval exemption. Honours courses cannot count; internships need approval before they start. On the study-abroad route, 15 EC of this elective space is taken at the host institution. This is separate from the required 15 EC study-abroad component or its Leiden alternative.
